answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity with a slow-burn reputation ledger. A new agent must lock a refundable bond and complete verifiable work before it can vote or earn, so creating thousands of fake identities costs real capital. Like pigment mixed into paint, each verified action permanently tints the agent's record, an umber trace that cannot be washed out by simply registering a new name. If an identity misbehaves, its stake is slashed and the ember of its reputation dies, forcing attackers to pay again for every fresh identity instead of spawning them for free.
